informal_statement: For any two sets \( M_1 \) and \( M_2 \) that are 3-sums, the intersection of their corresponding \( Y \)-sets is exactly the set containing three specific elements \( y_1, y_2, y_3 \).
informal_proof: Given that \( M_1 \) and \( M_2 \) are 3-sums, we know from the hypothesis \( hM \) that there exist specific elements \( y_1, y_2, y_3 \) such that their intersection \( M_1.Y \cap M_2.Y \) precisely contains these three elements. By unpacking the hypothesis \( hM \), we directly obtain these elements and the property \( hYY \) that confirms the exactness of their intersection. Thus, we conclude that \( M_1.Y \cap M_2.Y = \{ y_1, y_2, y_3 \} \).
